sn47.40:2.1: The term “development” shows that this takes the basic practice further.
sn47.40:2.2: This teaching on origination and vanishing is also found in [dn22:2.12](), [mn10:5.2](), and [sn52.1:3.1](). It is explained in the Samudayasutta at [sn47.42](). | The phrase _samudayadhamma_ (“liable to originate”) is found elsewhere as the realization of stream-entry ([sn56.11:11.2]()), and as a noble one’s discernment of the five aggregates ([sn22.126:2.1]()). Since both these speak of noble realization, it is reasonable to assume the current passage does too. The suffix _-dhamma_ indicates that this is not merely observing rise and fall, but is understanding the nature of things as dependently originated. | Grammatically, _samudayadhamma_ would normally be read as an adjective, but here it seems necessary to construe it as a noun (“liability to originate”), a construction also used at [sn23.21](). Bodhi also construes it as a noun: “nature of origination”.
